  How busy healthcare workers can use AI to make short study notes.
  Education support only, never advice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
IN THIS ISSUE
  * Notes, not wake-up calls

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES, NOT WAKE-UP CALLS

A quick story from an earlier life: for years at the bedside, education
meant getting handed a huge binder and a highlighter at the worst possible
hour. Learning does not have to feel like that.

AI can help you study between shifts, in small pieces, on your schedule.
But the boundary matters, so it is stated plainly: AI is education support
here. It is never medical advice, and this newsletter will never tell you
what to do for a patient or for yourself medically.

What AI is good at is the boring half of learning: restating things,
checking that your explanation is consistent, keeping your notes short and
calm, and making five minutes count.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE FIVE-MINUTE NOTE-SKETCH

Pick one small thing you learned this week - one workflow idea, one
systems concept, one thing that made your shift smoother. Ask an assistant
to restate it in three plain sentences.

Read those three sentences, fix the two that are wrong, and keep what is
left. That is a note that sticks, built by you, in five minutes.

This is education support. It is study hygiene, not clinical judgment -
and the judgment stays with the people whose job it is.

Link (dylanasdale.github.io - plain-English AI learning hub):
  https://dylanasdale.github.io/

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ONE THING WORTH YOUR TIME

Try one five-minute note-sketch this week: one thing you learned, restated
simply, corrected by you.
